blindReviewDeclaration: I received this checklist in a fresh subagent context, tried to falsify the current design, and wrote my findings and verdict before reading author self-review or author finding disposition.
expectedBehavior: The two generated registries form a disjoint 196-operation union; their commands partition to operations-admin=75, platform-admin=29, and public=9.

Every command has exactly one generated context kind; platform and public commands cannot receive a workspace grant, and a cross-kind invocation is rejected at compilation rather than by a runtime cast.
The numeric command baseline remains exactly 74 operations-admin normal branches plus five save branches, while the 34 platform/public commands are context-parity-only.
C5 and C6 are not fabricated numeric candidates: any C6 command readback remains in the command transaction with an owner-local bounded snapshot, never through a task reader.
BP-U01 through BP-U06 each bind to exactly one current design heading and the manifest keeps the reviewed hash.

round1FindingDispositions.evidence: Design section 4 now defines PLATFORM_COMMAND_CONTEXT and PUBLIC_PROTOCOL_CONTEXT and fixes the 75+29+9 partition, so the missing factory path is repaired. However OwnerOperationBindings.invoke(CommandContext, Object) accepts the sealed supertype at lines 104-118; a PlatformCommandContext or PublicProtocolCommandContext is assignable wherever a workspace binding is invoked. This contradicts the stated compile-fail cross-kind invariant at line 125 and leaves the binding boundary unable to enforce the repaired partition.

BP-U04 now supplies deterministic 75 operations-admin normal rows with save's normal branch replaced by five branches, yielding 74+5=79, and separately declares 29 platform plus 9 public parity-only rows. But it falsely classifies C6 as having no command consumer: CatalogOwnerService.dictionary is returned by the POST reorderOperationsCatalogDictionaryEntry command readback, so C6 lacks an honest command/readback impact and evidence disposition.

The current manifest binds BP-U01..BP-U06 to six distinct dedicated headings, each occurring exactly once in the reviewed design: lines 191, 195, 199, 203, 217, and 221. The manifest and design hashes equal the Round 2 fixed inputs.

findings.title: The repaired context partition is not compile-time safe at the generated binding boundary.
findings.evidence: The new sealed CommandContext correctly lists WorkspaceExecutionContext, WorkspaceProtocolContext, PlatformCommandContext, and PublicProtocolCommandContext, and section 4 assigns 75+29+9 commands to the kinds. Yet the sole OwnerOperationBindings command entry point is Object invoke(CommandContext context, Object command). Every kind is assignable to CommandContext, so a caller can invoke a workspace-bound branch with platform/public context and the declared cross-kind invocation cannot fail compilation. The current design allows runtime generated casts while claiming a compile-fail red fixture, which does not prove the stated isolation.
findings.risk: A generated callable boundary can accept a context from the wrong authorization domain. The implementation must either trust a runtime cast/failure or recreate an unchecked common dispatcher, breaking the design's platform/public versus workspace authority partition.
findings.disposition: Replace the shared callable command signature with generated kind-specific invocation interfaces or per-kind closed entry points whose parameter type is the exact context kind; retain Object only inside an immediately typed generated branch if needed. Add a real compile-fail fixture for passing PlatformCommandContext/PublicProtocolCommandContext to a workspace binding and the reciprocal cases.

findings.title: C6 is wrongly declared task-read-only although its N+1 path is returned from a command readback.
findings.evidence: BP-U04 lines 211-215 says C6 has no command and must not enter the command baseline, while BP-U05 line 219 forbids a task reader from command use. In current CatalogOwnerService, dictionary() performs dictionaryReferenced once per row (lines 528-533), and reorderDictionary() returns dictionary(...) after the POST mutation (line 784). The generated registry identifies reorderOperationsCatalogDictionaryEntry as a POST operations-admin catalog command. Therefore C6 is simultaneously a task-read and a command-readback concern, not a task-read-only candidate.
findings.risk: The design either leaves the command readback N+1 unresolved or calls a task reader inside the command transaction, which is explicitly forbidden. Its C1-C6 impact/evidence map would also omit the only command surface that exposes the C6 behavior.
findings.disposition: Keep the numeric 79 baseline cardinality unchanged because reorder is already one of its 74 normal operations, but amend C6 to name reorderOperationsCatalogDictionaryEntry and define an owner-local bounded dictionary-reference snapshot reusable by its command readback and the task-read handler. The shared helper must not be a TaskReadService call; add the command fixture and exact impact/evidence linkage before legacy retirement.

solutionReasonableness.problemFit: The current design's owner-local generated binding, transaction-local authorization facts, and per-operation measured baseline approach remains a proportionate response to repeated database round trips without deleting correctness work.
solutionReasonableness.simplerAlternativeAssessment: A dynamic shared dispatcher or a single permissive context would be smaller but violates static exact-set and authorization partitioning. The smallest sound repair is kind-specific generated invocation plus one owner-local bounded snapshot shared by C6's command readback and task-read paths.
solutionReasonableness.costFit: The two repairs are bounded design/generator changes; proceeding without them would either make the claimed compile-time safety false or preserve the C6 command N+1 under a misleading task-read-only label.

conclusion.summary: Round 2 independently verifies the unique-anchor repair and the 74+5=79 baseline arithmetic, and confirms platform/public factories are now explicitly modeled. It nevertheless finds two blocking residuals: the common CommandContext callable binding cannot enforce the promised cross-kind compile failure, and C6 incorrectly excludes the reorder dictionary command's N+1 readback. No implementation, runtime, seed/reset, L2/UAT, or repository-control action is authorized.
conclusion.authorizationBoundary: This is the final independent DESIGN round for this cycle. It authorizes no implementation, dynamic execution, seed/reset, L2/UAT, or repository-control action; further Codex adversarial review for this cycle is not allowed.
